correctness.rationale: For a fixed two-coordinate sum, the log ratio of the two Poisson-tail derivatives is strictly concave on the open half interval, ends at zero at the midpoint, and tends to minus infinity at the other endpoint. Its only possible interior sign change is from negative to positive, so every unequal positive split is strictly suboptimal to an endpoint or midpoint. Consequently all global optima have equal positive coordinates. The tail series gives elasticity r divided by a strictly increasing positive-coefficient series, decreasing from r to zero, and hence a unique density maximizer a_r. The adjacent objective ratio decreases strictly by the difference of these elasticities, with opposite signs relative to one at m a_r and (m+1)a_r. This orders every adjacent switch, giving exactly the claimed global winners and ties. For the limit with m fixed, the smaller Poisson mean is r+z sqrt(r) and its upper tail tends to Phi(z) by the Poisson CLT; the larger mean exceeds r by order r and gives tail tending to one by Chebyshev. Signs on either side of Phi^{-1}(m/(m+1)) trap the unique root. The tabulated four r=3 roots and the r=2 first root also agree with an independent gamma-function and Brent calculation.
residual_risks: The infinity notation B_{r,n} in the finite-n phase statement is a sentinel used only there, not the finite adjacent root with m=n from the unrestricted sequence; distinct notation would be clearer.
